1. Verify current-bill arithmetic: confirm meter reads (52,420 − 51,610 = 810 kWh), line-item sum ($18.38 + $21.31 + $108.87 = $148.56), and the total change versus last month ($148.56 − $154.52 = −$5.96). Flag any internal mismatch as a possible billing error.

2. Set price_usd: confirm both periods use the same AEP Ohio RS tariff (fixed $18.38/month; tier-1 variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh). Since published rates are unchanged between periods, price_usd = $0.00.

3. Set days_usd: both billing periods are 31 days; the customer charge is a flat monthly fee while energy and riders are billed per kWh, so day-count contributes nothing. days_usd = $0.00.

4. Estimate weather_usd: from NOAA history, compare last month (CDD 68.5, HDD 149.5, 847 kWh) with the current period (CDD 0, HDD 616.5, 810 kWh). Derive the weather-attributable kWh difference for this heating/cooling transition and value it at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

5. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd = −$5.96 exactly (i.e., value the non-weather kWh change at the variable rate).

6. Screen for a billing error: reconstruct the tariff total for 810 kWh ($18.38 + 810 × $0.1607225 ≈ $148.57), compare to the stated $148.56 and line items, and verify kWh against meter reads; the ~$0.01 gap is normal rounding, so billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

7. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
